A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dual Q-DM and the same analysis of IQ-Learn. Their complete main texts and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed subtitle, conference formatting, and renumbering. Figures, tables, equations, and retained proofs can be matched.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original experiments on the hard tabular instance and five MuJoCo tasks, with results in Figures 1-2.

after.justification: Original tabular and MuJoCo results remain, supplemented by Gridworld, demonstration-count, offline-training, and hyperparameter-sensitivity results in the main text and Appendix F.2.

M1.justification: The core constrained objective, Bellman penalty, architectures, and Algorithms 1-2 are retained. Value flow names the propagation mechanism already described in v1. The discounted theoretical formulation and experimental bound sweeps do not establish a replacement of the implemented base method.

E1.justification: v2 adds a Gridworld generalization case in Figure 1 and an explicit offline scenario for IQ-Learn variants on the retained MuJoCo tasks. The original hard tabular instance and all five MuJoCo tasks remain; demonstration-count sweeps do not add datasets.

E2.justification: ReCOIL joins the MuJoCo comparisons in Figures 2-3. Its underlying work was discussed in v1 but was not an evaluated comparator there. The existing MuJoCo and hard-instance comparator sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluation design with 1, 3, 5, and 7 demonstration trajectories, offline training using expert initial states and expert-only regularization, and Bellman-bound and penalty-coefficient sweeps. These are additional protocols; the original task-specific demonstration counts, listed hyperparameters, and ten-rollout evaluation procedure remain.

E4.justification: New analyses test several previously unexamined questions: Gridworld visualizes action selection outside demonstrations; Figure 3 tests demonstration efficiency; Figure 6 examines removing online interactions; and Figure 7 tests sensitivity to constraint bounds and penalty strength on HalfCheetah and Humanoid.

E5.justification: Both versions generally specify three independent seeds. v2 newly identifies Figure 6 as means with standard deviations over five seeds. This adds explicit uncertainty reporting for the offline experiment, but conflicts with the blanket three-run statement and does not establish increased runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds ReCOIL returns, demonstration-count results, Gridworld Q-value patterns, offline learning curves, and sensitivity results. New findings include poor offline performance for all three tested methods and sensitivity to extreme settings on Humanoid. The original hard-instance compounding-error trend remains; these additions are not evidence of a version-to-version performance gain.

T1.justification: New Appendix D develops the stationary discounted setting, including occupancy-flow constraints and discounted objectives. Theorems 3-4 and Propositions 4-5 extend the IQ-Learn/BC reduction and Dual Q-DM/AIL equivalence with proofs. The original finite-horizon results and technical lemmas are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: IQ-Learn reduces to BC, Dual Q-DM is equivalent to AIL, and Bellman constraints enable generalization and mitigation of compounding errors. The value-flow framing emphasizes propagation already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the added experiments as demonstrating superior demonstration efficiency and broad hyperparameter robustness, while acknowledging extreme-setting failures on Humanoid. The universal superiority wording in Section 6.2 is too strong: Figure 3 shows LS-IQ above Dual Q-DM on Hopper with one demonstration. The underlying propagation explanation is retained.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a Dual Q-DM implementation link and adds ReCOIL's source information and hyperparameters in Table 9. Appendix F.2 documents the new offline procedures and sweep ranges. Existing hardware, architectures, and Tables 3-8 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds discussion of importance-weighted BC from imperfect demonstrations and further references on AIL with function approximation and reward generalization. The central positioning against IQ-Learn and primal-dual IL remains. The stage-coupled AIL reference changes from its preprint to publication rather than becoming a new work.

P1.justification: The subtitle and mechanistic terminology shift to value flow. Section 3.2 moves the reparameterization argument before Theorem 1, Section 4.2 expands its explanatory narrative, and an impact statement is added. Appendices are renumbered and experimental details subdivided, while the main section sequence and much existing text remain.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text and references, with revised typography and running headers. It adds four figures and the ReCOIL hyperparameter table, updates comparison legends, and relocates existing displays. The original hard-instance plot and illustrative MDP become Figures 4 and 5.

improvement.justification: Appendix D addresses v1's finite-horizon restriction, while evaluating the closely related ReCOIL addresses an important comparison gap. The new generalization, offline, demonstration-count, and sensitivity experiments materially strengthen assessment of the proposed mechanism and practical behavior. The implementation link also improves reproducibility information. These gains outweigh localized weaknesses, including the overstated universal superiority claim in Figure 3's discussion and inconsistent three-run/five-seed reporting.
